speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I need to evaluate your systemic hypertension. To start, how old are you, and have you or your parents noticed any symptoms like headaches, blurred vision, or nosebleeds?

speaker: Patient
text: 5-year-old boy. The patient is presented by his mother for a well-child visit. The boy was born at 39 weeks gestation via spontaneous vaginal delivery, is currently up to date on all vaccines, and is meeting all developmental milestones. His mother reports that he has been generally doing well with no concerns. No family history of cardiovascular disease. The boy does not take any medications.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for that information. Since he is an asymptomatic 5-year-old with no family history, let's proceed with a physical exam. Please confirm his current blood pressure reading and whether the measurements were taken correctly (e.g., proper cuff size, seated position).

REQUEST TEST: Blood_Pressure_Reading
REQUEST TEST: Physical_Examination_Findings

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Blood_Pressure_Reading: 150/80 mm Hg (Right Upper Extremity); Physical_Examination_Findings: 2+ radial pulses and trace femoral pulses; Heart_Auscultation: Normal S1 and S2, 2/6 long systolic murmur with systolic ejection click over the left sternal border and back; Point_of_Maximal_Impact: Normal location.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The blood pressure is significantly elevated at 150/80 mm Hg, and the faint femoral pulses with a systolic murmur and click suggest coarctation of the aorta or coarctation syndrome. To confirm this, I need to see a cardiac imaging study.

REQUEST IMAGES: Echocardiogram

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is High blood pressure on the right upper extremity.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The discrepancy in blood pressure between your arms and legs, combined with weak femoral pulses and a murmur, strongly suggests a narrowing of the aorta. Do you have any history of a heart murmur or a "rib notching" sensation, and can you tell me if your mother has ever had surgery for an aortic issue?

DIAGNOSIS READY: Coarctation of the Aorta
